sentences.text: Animantarx was a slow-moving, four-legged herbivore covered in heavy armor but lacked a tail club. It had a skull about 25 cm long and a total body length of no more than 3 meters.

The name Animantarx means "living citadel" in Latin, referencing the animal's armored nature. This name honors paleontologist R.S. Lull's description of ankylosaurs as "living citadels" that were practically unassailable.

Only a single specimen of Animantarx has been discovered to date. Animantarx was the first dinosaur discovered using a radioactivity detection method. The species is named after Ramal Jones, who found the specimen using a modified Geiger counter in an area with no exposed bones.

Animantarx belongs to the family Nodosauridae and is classified as a member of the Ankylosauria order within that family. The parent group of the genus Animantarx is Nodosauridae. It belongs to the class Ornithischia.

Animantarx is classified as a nodosaurid ankylosaur, though its exact position within the family remains uncertain. Recent cladistic analyses of ankylosaurian phylogeny do not include Animantarx, leading researchers to classify the genus as incertae sedis within Nodosauridae based on its rounded supraorbital protuberances and a handle-shaped acromion on the scapula.

Animantarx lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 106 to 97 million years ago. Fossils found in mudstone alongside aquatic animals suggest Animantarx lived in a floodplain environment. It lived in what is now North America during the Cenomanian and Turonian stages, roughly 98 to 90 million years ago.

Recent analyses exclude Animantarx from the main ankylosaur tree, classifying it as Nodosauridae incertae sedis due to unique skull and shoulder features. Some studies suggest Animantarx is the closest relative of Edmontonia within the Nodosauridae family. Two separate studies have found that Animantarx is the closest relative of Edmontonia within the family Nodosauridae.
